newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: StorageTek sees growth in Asia.
newsitem.headline: StorageTek sees growth in Asia.

text.p: Data storage provider Storage Technology Corp. said Tuesday it planned to use Singapore as a hub for the rapidly expanding data storage business in Asia.

Bruce Taafe, vice-president for Asia Pacific operations, said Singapore was chosen as the company's first Asian office outside Japan because of its infrastructure, advanced application of information technology and proximity to key industry players.

"Our business model says we need direct operations in Singapore ... Singapore will become the hub of ASEAN (Association of Southeast Asian Nations) in the next two to three years," Taafe told a news conference.
A sales force will be developed in the first year, along with consulting services, he said.
The Louisville, Colo.-based company provides storage solutions in tape, disk and network products, as well as consultancy on storage management to government agencies and financial institutions.

StorageTek has more than an 80 percent share of the high-end tape storage market worldwide. Taafe said StorageTek in Asia would focus on data storage solutions for high-end mainframe users and personal computers.
The Asia-Pacific region accounts for about 8 percent of the company's revenue, but this is expected to increase to 20-25 percent in five years, Taafe said.
